I’ve been farming this land since I was fourteen, so I know every corner of my nine mu. My husband works part-time at a factory in town, and my son comes back to help at planting and harvest, but mostly it’s me running the farm. I used to grow wheat and summer maize like everyone else, but after my husband took the factory job we didn’t have the labor for that crazy week between wheat harvest and maize planting. So now I do spring maize and cotton — five mu of spring maize on the better-drained east field, and four mu of cotton on the west field where the soil holds moisture longer.

For seed, I buy hybrid maize seed, Denghai 605, from the input dealer in town. It costs about 45 yuan per mu, but everyone around here plants it and it gives good cobs. For cotton I use Lumianyan 27, an improved variety — I tried saving my own seed once and the yield dropped badly, so now I buy fresh every year. Before planting I rotary till both fields. My nephew brings his small tractor and charges 40 yuan per mu.

For fertilizer, I put down one bag of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer per mu for both crops — that’s 50 kg per mu. For the maize, I topdress with half a bag of urea, about 25 kg per mu, when the plants are knee-high. The extension fellow at the village meeting said 15 kg nitrogen per mu is enough, but last year when I cut back to save money the cobs were thin at the tips, so this year I’m putting a bit more. That comes to about 18 kg nitrogen, 7.5 kg phosphorus, and 7.5 kg potassium per mu for the maize. Cotton is hungrier because it grows all summer, so I give it a bit more urea at flowering and boll-set — almost a full bag split in two doses. All together that’s about 21 kg nitrogen, 8 kg phosphorus, and 8 kg potassium per mu for cotton.

Irrigation costs electricity, so I don’t water for nothing. The maize gets two times: once at jointing if June is dry, and once at grain filling in August. The cotton needs three times — at budding, flowering, and boll stage — because if the bolls dry out you lose your shirt. For chemicals, the maize gets one herbicide spray before emergence and two insecticide sprays later in summer. Cotton is where the money goes — I spray every seven to ten days through July and August, about thirteen times total, mostly for bollworm. If you miss even one spray the worms get inside the bolls and you can’t sell the cotton.

I expect about 1,100 kg per mu from the spring maize if the autumn rains come on time, and about 550 kg per mu of seed cotton. That’s roughly what I got last year, and my neighbors get about the same.
